articles.title_orig: iPhone 18 Pro vs. iPhone Duo: Comparing Apple’s New Pro Phone Against Its First Foldable
articles.title_zh: iPhone 18 Pro vs. iPhone Duo: Comparing Apple’s New Pro Phone Against Its First Foldable
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro is now on sale , but the foldable iPhone Duo is still awaiting its big debut on Oct. 23. While both phones are premium showstoppers, they’re also very different.
The 18 Pro features the company’s best camera yet on an iPhone , including a variable aperture for the first time. That feature helps you control light exposure, which can improve low-light photography, and you can use the new Pro Controls for additional features, like adjusting shutter speed. And while the outside is similar to the iPhone 17 Pro , the inside has been redesigned to accommodate a larger vapor chamber that helps keep the phone cool during intensive use.
But it’s the iPhone Duo that really captured people’s attention. It’s Apple’s first foldable phone , with a passport-style design that’s made to fit in your hand when closed. Then you can unfold it like a book to reveal a wide screen that’s almost the size of an iPad Mini (an open iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch screen while an iPad Mini measures 8.3 inches). Yet, it only has two rear cameras rather than the three that the 18 Pro has, so it won’t have a telephoto lens for zooming into a subject as far as the Pro and Pro Max can. It also doesn’t have the aforementioned variable aperture.
On top of that, the iPhone Duo is extremely expensive: It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB version. The iPhone 18 Pro isn’t cheap either, but it is less of a stretch, with a starting price of $1,199 for the 256GB version.
Here are the top highlights for each phone, and you can use our specs chart to compare them further.
The primary difference between the two phones lies in their designs. The iPhone 18 Pro has the usual slab iPhone design that we’ve come to know over the years. It even has the same dimensions as its predecessor, measuring 5.9 by 2.3 by 0.3 inches. This means you can use the same phone cases whether they were designed for the iPhone 17 Pro or the 18 Pro. The 18 Pro has an aluminum unibody design with a triple camera array on the back. On the front is a 6.3-inch OLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate. The display also includes a slimmer Dynamic Island cutout for the front-facing camera and Face ID, which can now display three Live Activities at once.
The iPhone Duo, on the other hand, is quite the departure from Apple as the company’s first foldable. Closed, it has rounded corners on the upper and lower right along with flat titanium sides. Due to its passport size, it has a rather squat 5.4-inch cover display on the front. When it’s closed, it measures 4.6 by 3.3 by 0.4 inches.
Open the Duo up, and you will see a 7.6-inch OLED display. While the cover screen has the usual glossy glass display of other iPhones, the main internal display of the iPhone Duo has a matte nano-textured finish designed to reduce reflections and minimize the appearance of the crease. Also, when the Duo is open, it’s just 0.2 inches thick, which is even thinner than last year’s iPhone Air (0.22 inches). Both displays support a 120Hz refresh rate, and the phone can use StandBy mode widgets when folded into a tent-like position. The iPhone Duo doesn’t have Face ID and instead uses a side fingerprint sensor for Touch ID unlocking.
Both phones are IP68-rated for dust and water resistance. That’s particularly notable for the Duo, as it’s one of the few book-style foldable phones to carry that rating. (Google’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold and 11 Pro Fold are also rated IP68.)
The iPhone 18 Pro has the best camera features that Apple has to offer. It has a triple rear camera array: a 48-megapixel wide, ultrawide and telephoto. Its new variable aperture, lets you control how much light hits the sensor, allowing for improved low-light photography, greater depth-of-field for close-up shots and overall a lot more flexibility for creative photography.
While the iPhone Duo has a compact foldable design as its spotlight feature, its camera system harkens more to what’s included on the iPhone 17 . Despite being substantially more expensive than the iPhone 18 Pro, the Duo has a 48-megapixel wide camera and a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera. It does not have a telephoto camera, but its camera system does allow for a 2x optical quality zoom along with a digital zoom to 10x. It also does not have the variable aperture that’s included on the 18 Pro.
Both phones have selfie cameras; the 18 Pro has a 18-megapixel front-facing camera, while the Duo has a 12-megapixel Center Stage selfie camera on the cover display as well as a hidden under-display FaceTime camera on the main display. The benefit of the Duo, however, is that you can actually use the 48-megapixel rear camera as your “selfie” camera when the phone is open as the cover display becomes a viewfinder.
Both phones ship with Apple’s latest A20 Pro chip, which is the company’s first to be made with a 2-nanometer process. The processor is therefore denser and should result in a 20% faster CPU and a 40% faster GPU than last year’s A19 Pro. It should also help keep the phone cool even during intensive use.
As for battery life, Apple doesn’t give the specific capacity for both phones, but it does say that the 18 Pro should last up to 24 hours, while the iPhone Duo will last up to 44 hours while watching videos when closed, and up to 31 hours when open.
In our preliminary test with the 18 Pro, we found that it lasted almost a full day before needing to be charged. It’s also one of the fastest-charging phones CNET has tested, charging from 0% to 82% in just 30 minutes. According to Apple, the iPhone Duo will charge to 50% in about 15 minutes with a 60-watt charger, or to 50% in 30 minutes with a 35-watt wireless MagSafe charger. We’ll have to perform further tests to be sure.

articles.title_orig: Philly teacher, activist admits she lied for years about being Palestinian and Black
articles.title_zh: Philly teacher, activist admits she lied for years about being Palestinian and Black
articles.content_orig:

Hannah Gann, an activist and 10th grade social studies teacher at the Workshop School in West Philadelphia, shown above, confessed that she has lied for years about being Palestinian and Black. Gann, a white woman of Jewish descent, issued an apology after activist groups confronted her and exposed the deception.
A white Philadelphia teacher is under fire for falsely claiming for years that she was a Black woman of Palestinian descent. She now admits she duped organizers in the city and undermined the racial justice causes that she had long fought for as a member of activist groups.
Hannah Gann, an educator at the Workshop School, a public magnet high school in West Philly, acknowledged her deception in a series of social media posts in recent days.
"I lied about my identity and have been lying for years," Gann wrote on Instagram. "I have no Palestinian or Tunisian heritage. I am a white woman of significant privilege and wealth. Anyone who supported me was manipulated and should not be judged as a result of their support for me."
Gann's deception has drawn comparisons to the story of Rachel Dolezal, a white civil rights activist and college instructor who posed as a Black woman for years and became the president of the NAACP chapter in Spokane, Washington, before she was exposed in 2015.
The local Racial Justice Organizing Committee and Philly Educators for Palestine addressed the fallout of Gann's fabrication in a joint statement over the weekend. The groups confronted Gann last week following an investigation into her background. They said Gann claimed at various times to be Palestinian, Tunisian and Black.
After a discussion with Gann on Thursday, the groups said she admitted she is a white woman of Jewish heritage who comes from an Israeli settler family.
"We are stunned, saddened and angered by this betrayal," the groups said in a statement. "We will no longer work with Hannah, and she will no longer be welcome in any of our organizing protests."
Gann's pro-Palestinian activism over the years has drawn the ire of right-wing foes, including one group that parked a mobile billboard outside her school in February 2024 that showed a picture of her wearing a keffiyeh and displayed the words, "Hannah Gann: 10th Grade Teacher & Philadelphia’s Leading Antisemite.”
School district spokesperson Monique Braxton said the district is aware of the social media posts "concerning a district employee and her involvement with an outside advocacy organization." Braxton said the district is making support available to students and staff at the Workshop School, but said the district would not comment on personnel matters or any possible discipline.
"These posts reference the employee's involvement in an external group," Braxton said.
In a lengthy video posted to Instagram, Gann apologized and lamented that her conduct has become "a sick, deluded distraction" from the causes she supported under false pretenses.
"One of the most sickening aspects of facing what I've done is seeing the way that the blowback is falling on people, groups, communities and causes I genuinely care about," Gann said. "I recognize it's far too late for me to mitigate all the damage I've done, but I'm determined to try to do what I can."
A post shared by Hannah Gann (@ms.gann.on.the.gram)
Gann claimed she never compromised the safety of any of the organizations and people she stood with and was not working on behalf of groups opposed to their causes.
"One of the ways I justified my unjustifiable deceptions was by telling myself that it was OK because I only lied about myself," Gann said. "If I ever spoke on something publicly, taught it at a political education event or shared learning resources, they were always as true and as genuine as I could ensure."
Gann also said she lied to everyone in her life about her background, including her own family.
"Maybe one day I'll make a video explaining what was going through my mind, how I allowed half-truths and obfuscations to grow into outright lies, how genuinely I wanted to commit to the work I was doing in spite of those lies," she said.
Gann specifically addressed her longtime friendship with fellow Philadelphia teacher Keziah Ridgeway, who was disciplined by the School District of Philadelphia for her pro-Palestinian activism and has since sued the school district . Gann has worked alongside Ridgeway over the years, including organizing a teach-in to protest Israel's destruction of schools in Gaza, and Gann has publicly defended Ridgeway amid her legal battle. Gann said Ridgeway had no knowledge that she had lied about her heritage.
Ridgeway, who has faced scrutiny over Gann's deception, posted a video this week detailing the history of their friendship. Ridgeway said she met Gann in 2018 and only discovered she had been lying about her ancestry when approached by other activists. For years, Ridgeway said she saw no reason to doubt Gann's credibility.
"What we saw from her was she was doing the work," Ridgeway said. "She was speaking up for the Black community. She was speaking up for the Palestinian community, and that is what we took as the important thing."
A member of the Philly Palestine Coalition informed Ridgeway earlier this month that organizers were suspicious about Gann's background and had done research to prove she was not telling the truth. Ridgeway said Gann denied the allegations when she was confronted and only admitted what she had done after relentless questioning.
"I acted when I had concrete evidence, and it is because I acted that she posted that public statement," Ridgeway said.
The Racial Justice Organizing Committee and Philly Educators for Palestine said Gann's admission "is not accountability" and that they are reviewing her access to organizational information and resources she received through the misrepresentation of her identity.
"We recognize the profound harm this has caused; Palestinians whose identity and struggle were appropriated; the Black community, young people, organizers, and organizations whose trust and resources were exploited, as well as those who supported Hannah based on false information," the statement said. "We hope that support will not be used to discredit the people who acted in good faith."
Gann asked those who viewed her video not to take their anger and disappointment out on others.
"No one should be blamed or judged for their association with me," Gann said.

articles.title_orig: Exploring Giants quarterback options with Jaxson Dart sidelined for rest of regular season
articles.title_zh: Exploring Giants quarterback options with Jaxson Dart sidelined for rest of regular season
articles.content_orig:
What was originally believed to be a minor multi-week MCL sprain has completely derailed the New York Giants season, leaving the fanbase reeling after head coach John Harbaugh's optimistic press conference blew up in their faces. Tune in for Craig Carton's unfiltered breakdown of how the Giants botched the injury narrative and where the franchise goes from here.
When New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury this week, we knew there'd be two reactions from the overwhelmingly liberal sports media.
First, they'd call for the Giants to sign Colin Kaepernick . They do it whenever an NFL team loses a quarterback, even though Kaepernick has not played professional football in a decade.
Second, they'd mock Dart’s injury because he made headlines in May by introducing President Donald Trump at a New York City event.
Both reactions materialized almost immediately.
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and President Donald Trump shake hands during an event inside Eugene Levy Fieldhouse at Rockland Community College in Suffern, N.Y., on Friday, May 22, 2026. Trump spoke about his economic accomplishments in the toss-up congressional district represented by Rep. Mike Lawler, who is up for reelection in one of the most closely watched congressional races in the November midterm elections. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)
DAN LE BATARD DEMANDS THE MEDIA MAKE JAXSON DART 'UNCOMFORTABLE' FOR INTRODUCING TRUMP
Sports blogger Mike Florio was the first to urge the Giants to sign Kaepernick . Elsewhere, the usual suspects framed Dart's injury as political karma.
"Media types say 'Trump Curse' has struck again," wrote HuffPost in an article referring to Dart as a "Trump admirer."
"The f—–g Trump curse strikes again," wrote Tara Setmayer, a former GOP communications director on Capitol Hill and CNN commentator, about Dart’s injury on X.
Film and TV critic John Rocha shared a photo of Trump and Dart’s interaction, writing, " Everything he touches, y'all . Everything he touches..."
Ron Filipkowski, the partisan editor of the anti-Trump outlet MeidasTouch, claimed he had predicted Dart’s injury after the quarterback appeared with Trump.
"This was the moment I decided not to draft Dart in fantasy football. He had no chance this season after the Trump Curse," he wrote above a clip of Dart and Trump.
Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants walks off the field after a play against the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) (Harry How/Getty Images)
THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!
Other outlets adopted a similar tone.
"Jaxson Dart's injury reignites Trump sports curse possibility," joked USA Today.
The people making these jokes will insist they are harmless. Perhaps some of them believe that. But they know exactly what they are doing and how their majority anti-Trump audiences will respond.
Look at the comments under The Athletic’s report about Dart’s season-ending injury. The comment section resembles a fringe political message board, with readers celebrating the injury, asking whether Dart is "vaxxed" and claiming that he deserves this because he supported Trump.
Interestingly, we do not know whether Dart is a Trump supporter.
Yes, he introduced Trump at an event. But introducing the sitting president is not, on its face, a political statement. The event also took place in the city where Dart plays quarterback. For all we know, Dart would have accepted the same opportunity if a Democrat were in the White House.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic, OpenAI CEOs warn AI could threaten humanity without safeguards
articles.title_zh: Anthropic, OpenAI CEOs warn AI could threaten humanity without safeguards
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman warns about the risks associated with artificial intelligence during a speech at the United Nations.
The CEOs of two of the world's leading AI companies warned the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday that rapidly advancing AI could threaten humanity if governments and industry fail to keep it under human control.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said AI has enormous potential but also carries significant risks if it is not developed responsibly.
"If managed poorly, I even believe AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole," Amodei told the 15-member council during a special meeting on AI held alongside the U.N. General Assembly.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delivered a similar warning, saying AI's development could move "so fast" that humans no longer have the ability to understand or intervene.
SAM ALTMAN IDENTIFIES TWO BIGGEST RISKS FACING AI'S FUTURE
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman looks on during a UN Security Council meeting on artificial intelligence during the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York on Sept. 23, 2026. (Angela Weiss/AFP via Getty Images)
"We could lose control of the future to AI," Altman said. "The risk is that it moves so fast that people can no longer follow what's happening or intervene when needed. This would obviously be terrible."
The meeting comes as concerns grow over increasingly advanced AI systems.
"For all the differences of the people in this room, we must put aside those differences in order to confront this global opportunity and global threat that is being presented to us at the same time," Amodei said. "No leader, no company and no nation can manage this alone."
EMPLOYEES AT AI COMPANIES BACK BERNIE SANDERS BILL CRACKING DOWN ON DEVELOPMENT
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei appears virtually during a United Nations Security Council meeting at the U.N. General Assembly in New York on Sept. 23, 2026. (John Lamparski/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Altman also urged countries to work together on AI as the technology continues to advance.
"If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone," he said. "They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments, accountable to the people that they serve. At the international level, this will require cooperation."
He added, "In our history, there have been times where countries who compete and don't always like each other very much still come together for shared interests and the collective good in the face of a powerful new technology. We believe this must be one of those times."
TRUMP REBRANDS AI, REJECTS 'GLOBALIST SCHEME' TO CONTROL TECH
Yoshua Bengio, one of the 'Godfathers' of AI, discusses the threats of frontier AI models during a speech at the United Nations.
The debate over how to develop and govern AI has intensified in recent weeks.
Earlier this month, Amodei published an essay urging the industry to "slow the pace" of frontier AI development. The essay drew public support from Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
The discussion at the U.N. also came a day after President Donald Trump said the U.S. would reject what he described as a "globalist scheme" to control AI, while emphasizing that the U.S. should remain the global leader in the technology.
French Foreign Ministry spokesperson Pascal Confavreux told Fox News Digital in an interview that France is seeking to bring artificial intelligence to the center of international security discussions, with a special UN Security Council meeting on Wednesday featuring executives from OpenAI, Anthropic and Hugging Face.
"For a few weeks now, we wanted to bring AI at the center stage," Confavreux said, explaining that the meeting was the first of its kind to feature briefers at this level from leading AI companies.
He said recent cybersecurity concerns, including a reported hacking incident involving Hugging Face, underscore the need to address AI-related security risks at the international level.
"We need to bring that into the discussions of the global community," he said.
The meeting was chaired by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, alongside the Security Council's 14 other members.

articles.title_orig: ‘Brothers’ Rotten Tomatoes Reviews Split Over McConaughey And Harrelson Comedy
articles.title_zh: ‘Brothers’ Rotten Tomatoes Reviews Split Over McConaughey And Harrelson Comedy
articles.content_orig:
The actors co-star in a lightly fictionalised meta-comedy about their real-life bromance – and possible sharing of parents. It’s a tasty little treat
T he cheek! The indulgence! The privilege! Did anyone, anywhere in 2026, look up from news of a world in flames and say, what we really need now is a meta-comedy where two actors play gently self-satirising fictional versions of themselves?
They did not, and yet here are Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson. They once co-starred in the first season of True Detective , one of TV’s darkest and best crime dramas, but otherwise their personae have them as lifelong besties who are both free spirits, unencumbered by the rules of the fame game – not the sort of chaps who would stop and think about how their self-referential comedy bagatelle might be received. In Brothers, they portray themselves as blokes who don’t stop and think, full stop.
We begin in Malibu at Harrelson’s sea-view mansion, where we see him army-crawling past the infinity pool in an effort not to be seen by his wife and daughters, because he has detected the sound of the thing he fears most, raw female feelings. Sure enough, once he’s been spotted and captured, it turns out that his elder daughter Olive (Highdee Kuan) has suffered a collapsed engagement and the family is in crisis. So he implements the only solution he can come up with given his lack of emotional intelligence, which is to bundle his women into his converted bus and road-trip to the Texas hilltop homestead of his old buddy, Matthew McConaughey . The wide plains and wide-armed Texas welcome will heal all.
When he gets there, though, he finds McConaughey agonising over a speech he’s giving at an event commemorating his venerated late father. The introspection, and the possibility of showing himself to be an inspiring orator sparks a midlife-crisis plan to run for election as state governor. The presence of Harrelson, a house guest who has arrived unbidden and does not know when to leave, is a complication, even before Harrelson has a bomb dropped on him in a private conversation with McConaughey’s mother: she used to know Harrelson’s dad, and that’s “know” in the sense that he might also have been McConaughey’s father.
The two pals reconnect over such staples of Texas life as huntin’, fishin’, rodeo-ridin’ and returning from a car journey with the bloody corpse of the deer you ran over strapped to the roof. The mild culture clash between the straight-talking Texan McConaugheys and the angsty Californian Harrelsons causes beef that’s easily sorted with huggin’ and learnin’ at the episode’s end – albeit with the potentially cow-sized beef of the two men’s secret genetic link rumbling through the season.
It sounds inessential, and it is, but hock-bobbit and skippity-breakfast if this pair of toot-scootin’ Hollywood butt-nuts haven’t hit upon a tasty little comedy dynamic. Their screen personalities are different but the same in ways that can never be resolved, which is just what a comedy wants. McConaughey is a man of faith, in God and “the universe”, whose conservative ways are at odds with Harrelson’s west-coast liberalism, but Harrelson’s environmental awareness and animal-rights principles are also articles of blind faith. Harrelson seems selfish and insensitive compared with McConaughey’s convivial mateyness, but his bluntness often shakes his friend out of the fantasy world he lives in. Both are all hat and no cattle, but each can only see that in the other, not in themselves.
The fake screen Harrelson and the exaggerated fictional McConaughey are, in other words, strong sitcom protagonists. Even better, though, are the supporting players, starting with Holland Taylor as the aforementioned loose-lipped matriarch, Ma Mac, a self-described “woman of quality” who occasionally has a shotgun in one hand and always has a drink in the other. “This isn’t a draaaaaank ,” she tells Harrelson: “This is my mornin’ coffee ‘n Kahlúa! There’s barely any vodka in here!”
Fiercely competing with Taylor for the show’s best scene-stealer is Lisa Gilroy as McConaughey’s campaign manager, a power-suited dispenser of unvarnished honesty. “I love the folksy spirit of this!” she says, waving a hand at her client, as he rambles on about his down-home family values. “Not personally. Personally I find it repulsive. But for the campaign? It’s gold!” Or to McConaughey’s patient wife Valentina (a somewhat thankless role for Natalie Martinez): “I love you playing the role of this cool, level-headed spouse, it really works for you. I am going to get you a stylist though, because the dress you’re wearing? It’s made of jeans. And I’m going to get you a good hairbrush. Hey Siri! Remind me to get the wife a good hairbrush!”
Such fine creations further down the cast show that Brothers is a bit more than two famous guys blithely horsing around, even if that’s what it ultimately boils down to. It’s a fun little trip.

articles.title_zh: Qualcomm announces Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 for AI 'hearables,' even ones with cameras
articles.content_orig:
Qualcomm announced the Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 as a substantial chipset for upcoming audio devices, with a massive focus on better AI performance for audio wearables.
The Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 SoC is purpose-built for audio wearables, or “hearables” as Qualcomm puts it in its press release. With the push beyond simple audio performance, the chipmaker is taking the opportunity to build on what audio chipsets can do, as far as contextual image recognition for any camera-equipped earbuds the new chipset might be used in.
As for pure performance, Qualcomm notes the new Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 will be capable of up to 2x greater on-device AI performance. That comes at a lower power consumption rate by up to 40%. Translated to real-world use, the SoC is poised for AI wearables with local and online models that should require less frequent charges. Android XR devices would be a key example, since Gemini will need to live locally and gather information from real-world surroundings.
The chipset is also capable of Wi-Fi 6E, so OEMs can position devices to offer on-board or cloud-based AI access.
Qualcomm hasn’t abandoned the core principles of the audio chipsets. The Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 will have aptX and XPAN connectivity for better audio quality and Bluetooth range. But it will also leverage AI performance for better ANC built on Qualcomm’s 5th-generation protocol.
The chipmaker goes on to list a few theoretical devices the new SoC would be able to power. Some examples are traditional earbuds and headphones, as well as “open-ear hybrid audio designs, camera-enabled devices, audio glasses, and future multimodal wearables.”
Qualcomm doesn’t mention any key upcoming devices the Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 SoC chipset would live in, but with Android XR devices and more coming from large companies, it likely won’t be long before the new silicon is undergoing real-world use.

articles.title_orig: Brand-New M6 Mac mini Starts at $879.99 at Amazon
articles.title_zh: Brand-New M6 Mac mini Starts at $879.99 at Amazon
articles.content_orig:
The new Mac mini is the kind of Mac upgrade Apple has done a million times. It’s the same design as before but with new guts.
These play-it-safe updates aren’t very exciting, but they’re also usually all upside—you get a year or two’s worth of technological improvements for the same price you would have paid for the older version yesterday. Unfortunately, 2026’s unprecedented memory crunch has upended that standard operating procedure.
The new Mac mini starts at $899 for a version with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, a $300 increase for the same memory and storage specs you could get in the $599 M4 Mac mini in 2024.
The M4 Mac mini was a great general-purpose desktop computer and one of the best values Apple had ever offered in a desktop Mac. The M6 Mac mini is only one of those things. I’ll let you guess which.
Note that this review is specifically for the M6 version of the Mac mini. We didn’t get an M5 Pro Mac mini to review, but we’ll talk more about how its pricing and performance fits in for our Mac Studio review.
The M4 Mac minis gave the computers their first full redesigns in nearly 15 years, so it’s not too surprising that the new Mac minis don’t change anything. Compared to the older Intel and M1/M2-era versions, they’re slightly taller (2 inches, up from 1.4), but they have a smaller 5×5-inch footprint (down from 7.7 inches squared). The system is actively cooled, with a fan vent on the bottom to make sure that whatever chip is inside can run at high sustained clock speeds (passively cooled Apple Silicon Macs like the MacBook Air have always been a bit slower than actively cooled Macs with the same chip).
All Mac minis have two 10 Gbps USB-C ports and a headphone jack on the front, and a 2.5 Gbps (default) or 10 Gbps (optional) Ethernet port and HDMI port on the back. Both also have three Thunderbolt ports on the back, but these are Thunderbolt 4 on the M6 Mac mini and Thunderbolt 5 on the M5 Pro version. That means the M6 mini’s ports top out at 40 Gbps, while the M5 Pro mini supports up to 120 Gbps speeds.
Realistically, there aren’t a ton of things on a Mac that can use all that bandwidth, especially since Apple doesn’t support external GPUs. But you do need a Thunderbolt 5 Mac to daisy-chain multiple computers together to form a compute cluster, so if that’s something you’re interested in, keep it in mind when you buy—maybe you’re buying multiple desktops, or maybe you already have an M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro you’d like to test the feature with.
The only real gripe with this design continues to be its bottom-rear-mounted power button; apparently, complaints about this are being sent to the same trash can Apple has always used for complaints about the Magic Mouse’s bottom-mounted charging port. It doesn’t come up often in everyday use if you just let your Mac go to sleep rather than shutting it down. But the positioning problem does really call attention to itself when you pair a TouchID-equipped external keyboard with the mini, since it requires a quick double-tap of the Mac’s power button before the sensor will work.
Apple’s first M6-series chip is making its debut in the humble Mac mini, and the chip looks like the biggest upgrade Apple’s lower-end chip has gotten since the M4 generation added extra efficiency cores.
The headliner is the presence of two of Apple’s so-called “Super” cores , Apple’s nomenclature for P-cores that are even faster than its typical P-cores. Those are added on top of four P-cores and six E-cores for a total of 12 CPU cores. M4 and M5 both had 10 CPU cores. In the M4, these were split between four regular P-cores and six E-cores, whereas the M5 split them between four super cores and six E-cores (the M5’s cores were referred to as P-cores when it launched but were rebranded later when the M5 Pro and Max came out). The M1, M2, and M3 generations all used four P-cores and four E-cores.
The M6 has fewer super cores than the M5 but the same number of E-cores and four additional P-cores. While they’re apparently no longer “super,” the P-cores still perform well enough to ensure that the M6’s multi-core performance is better than M5’s overall.
Apple has mixed super cores with both other kinds of cores before, but this is its first chip to include all three kinds at once. To get around the awkwardness this might create at the CPU scheduler level, the built-in powermetrics tool suggests that Apple is still treating the M6 like a chip with just two types of cores. The six E-cores are all gathered together in one cluster, and the two Super cores and the four P-cores are all lumped together into a second six-core cluster called the “PS cluster.”
Powermetrics also reports that both the P- and S-cores have the same peak and minimum clock speeds, unlike in the M5 Pro and M5 Max where they’re different clusters with different clock speeds (both P- and S-cores in M6 range from 1.44 GHz to 4.79 GHz). The sysctl utility also suggests they share the same 20MB pool of L2 cache, up from 16MB for the 4-core Super cluster in the M5 (the E-core cluster has a bit more L2 cache, too, 8MB up from 6MB in the M5). The Super cores do have more L1 instruction and data cache, so they are definitely still different cores, and there are likely other differences that we can’t detect using software-level tools. But if you were wondering how macOS was going to treat a chip with three different kinds of CPU cores at a software level, the answer is “to act like it still has two different kinds of cores.”
The M6 gets additional GPU cores for the first time since the M2, increasing the count from 10 cores to 12. These cores include improved versions of the integrated neural accelerators Apple introduced in the M5-series GPU for speeding up AI and machine-learning workloads like ray-tracing and MetalFX upscaling. A “Dual 16-core Neural Engine” also bumps the number of Neural Engine cores from 16 to 32. Saying you have 2×16 of something strikes me as a roundabout way of saying you have 32 of something, but I suppose the end result is the same either way.
One small wrinkle in the M6 variants the Mac mini uses: The basic 16GB Mac mini offers 153 GB/s of memory bandwidth, the same amount as the M5. The 24GB and 32GB versions offer 170 GB/s, an 11 percent increase that should marginally improve graphics performance and the speed of any local AI models you run on this machine. Our review unit is the 24GB version.
What of the M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra? If the rumors are true, the M6 could end up being a lonely chip.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple isn’t planning a full M6 chip generation and that it could skip directly to M7 branding for the Pro, Max, and Ultra chips. That would be a first for the company, which skipped shipping an M4 Ultra but has otherwise shipped a baseline, Pro, and Max-series chip in each generation so far.
But it makes sense for a couple of reasons. The first is that most of the M6’s gains can be attributed to its extra CPU and GPU cores relative to the M5, and the M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra all obviously still have more of both kinds of cores than the M6 does. The second is that it’s still pretty early for TSMC’s 2 nm process, following three generations where Apple used versions of TSMC’s 3 nm process, and Apple is probably fighting with every other fabless chipmaker on Earth to reserve capacity. Apple could be sticking with smaller, simpler 2 nm chips for now and saving its bigger and more complex chips for later, when capacity will be higher, yields will be better, and costs may be lower.
The new mini re-uses the launch strategy for last year’s Mac Studios, which used an M4 Max in the base model and an M3 Ultra in the top-tier configurations. The basic Mac mini uses the brand-new M6, while the semi-professional Mac mini tier gets the M5 Pro that we saw in MacBook Pros back in the spring .
This means the M6 mini has newer tech than the more-expensive M5 Pro mini—and marginally better single-core CPU performa

articles.title_zh: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington as US, China agree to extend trade truce
articles.content_orig:
China’s Xi visits US as Trump bets on stabilising global relations
United States President Donald Trump has welcomed his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping to Washington, DC, for a three-day visit and high-stakes talks on trade, Taiwan and artificial intelligence.
Xi’s landed at Joint Base Andrews, outside the US capital, on Wednesday as the Trump administration announced that the two countries have agreed to extend an 11-month trade deal that offered temporary relief from punishing tariffs.
Trump took the rare step of personally meeting Xi on his arrival, marking the first time in 11 years that a US president has greeted a foreign leader at the base, according to US media.
At the arrival ceremony, the leaders and their wives shook hands, spoke for a few minutes and stood for pictures as a military band played, cannons blasted and a B-1 military bomber flew overhead.
In a written statement afterwards, Xi said China and the US should be partners and not rivals, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. “He said that the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, complement each other and benefit the world,” Xinhua reported.
Trump’s in-person greeting signals the significance that Washington ascribes to its relationship with Beijing , whose meteoric economic rise over the last several decades has transformed it into a global superpower capable of rivalling the US.
Xi’s visit comes after he hosted Trump in Beijing in May.
His schedule in Washington, DC, will include a state dinner attended by leaders of the US’s powerful tech industry , a military ceremony at the White House and a visit to the National Archives, home to documents of historical and cultural significance such as the US Constitution and the Declaration of Independence.
His talks with Trump are likely to cover the US-Israel war on Iran, the US-China trade deal, AI , and US ties to Taiwan , the self-governing island that China claims as part of its territory, according to analysts.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday that he had met with Chinese ‌Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of Xi’s visit to “see if we could ⁠do a bigger deal as opposed to just a series ⁠of smaller things”.
“We have agreed today that we will extend what we call the Busan Agreement,” Bessent said.
The agreement, which was set to expire on November 10, has now been extended to January 10, he said.
Yun Sun, a senior fellow and director of the China Program at the Stimson Center, said the short extension suggests the two nations were planning a wider deal.
“The two sides indeed have a bigger scope of negotiation coming to their trade deals, and they need more time to negotiate the technicalities,” she told Al Jazeera, adding that the truce was expected to hold even before the trip began.
Sun called Xi’s visit to the US “unprecedented”, saying “there has never been any precedent in the history of US-China relations for the top two leaders of the two countries to visit each other within a single year”. She described the stabilisation of ties as “quite prominent and very impressive”, noting that only 12 months ago, the two countries were escalating tariffs and export controls against each other.
On Taiwan, Sun said Beijing’s main goal would be to prevent or stall a $14bn arms package that Congress approved earlier this year, but the Trump administration has been unwilling to advance.
She said she expected the most progress on AI, where the two governments could agree on ways to manage their dialogue.
“We know that the US has proposed a hotline mechanism for notification to each other when there is a significant security risk associated with AI that happens in their individual country,” she said. “We’ll have to see whether the two leaders are able to make progress on this important issue.”
